content.value_statement: Dynamic pages often hide data behind clicks, forms, and login flows. This skill helps teams choose and scope Firecrawl /interact integrations.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to use Firecrawl /interact instead of /scrape.
Identifies product patterns that need clicks, forms, filters, or pagination.
Recommends keeping browser workflows narrow and specific.
Covers persistent profiles for authenticated state when truly needed.
Links to language-specific Firecrawl documentation for implementation work.
limitations: It does not include executable SDK examples in the skill file.
It requires current Firecrawl documentation before writing integration code.
Hosted Firecrawl requests need a valid FIRECRAWL_API_KEY.
Open-ended browser automation may require a separate browser sandbox.

use_cases.title: Dynamic Search Results
use_cases.description: Plan an /interact flow for search forms, filters, and paginated results that plain scraping cannot reach.

use_cases.title: Authenticated Product Data
use_cases.description: Decide when persistent browser profiles are needed for login-gated dashboards or account-specific tools.

use_cases.title: AI Web Workflow Integration
use_cases.description: Scope browser actions before extraction so an agent can complete a focused web task safely.

prompt_templates.title: Choose the Firecrawl Method
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner triage for a new page
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this page behavior: [describe page]. Tell me whether /scrape is enough or /interact is needed, and explain why.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Browser Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design the smallest Firecrawl /interact workflow for this task: [goal]. Include clicks, form inputs, navigation, and stop conditions.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare an SDK Integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Using the current Firecrawl docs for [language], outline how to add /interact to this product flow: [flow details].

prompt_templates.title: Harden an Authenticated Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this authenticated /interact design: [design]. Identify profile, credential, sandbox, and scope risks before implementation.

output_examples.input: A catalog loads more products only after clicking a Load more button.
output_examples.output: Use /interact for the button clicks, then extract the expanded product list after the page reaches a stable state.

output_examples.input: A dashboard shows charts only after login and several filter changes.
output_examples.output: Use a scoped authenticated workflow. Consider persistent profiles only if session state must continue across runs.

output_examples.input: A static article page has all content in the first response.
output_examples.output: Stay with /scrape. The page can be read directly, so browser interaction adds unnecessary complexity.

best_practices: Start with /scrape, then escalate to /interact only when page actions are required.
Keep every interaction flow narrow, deterministic, and tied to a product goal.
Read the language-specific Firecrawl source-of-truth page before writing code.
anti_patterns: Using /interact for pages that can be read directly with /scrape.
Creating open-ended browser automation without evaluating sandbox needs.
Placing API keys in prompts, source files, logs, or shared transcripts.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps developers plan Firecrawl /interact integrations for dynamic pages that need browser actions before extraction.

faq.question: Does the skill run browser actions by itself?
faq.answer: No. It is guidance for product code that calls Firecrawl APIs.

faq.question: When should I use /interact instead of /scrape?
faq.answer: Use /interact when content appears only after clicks, typing, navigation, filters, pagination, or login flows.

faq.question: Is a Firecrawl API key required?
faq.answer: Hosted Firecrawl requests require FIRECRAWL_API_KEY. Self-hosted deployments may also use a custom FIRECRAWL_API_URL.

faq.question: Which implementation languages are referenced?
faq.answer: The skill links to Firecrawl docs for Node, TypeScript, Python, Rust, Java, Elixir, cURL, and REST.

faq.question: Can it support authenticated workflows?
faq.answer: Yes. It notes persistent profiles for cases that truly need authenticated state across sessions.
